Yes, **your Neovim theme directly controls code coloring**. 

A colorscheme dictates which colors are applied to every part of your code (keywords, strings, functions, variables, types, comments, etc.). If a theme (such as `ravenswing` in your config) does not define highlights for Neovim's modern Tree-sitter capture groups (`@function`, `@keyword`, `@variable`, `@string`, etc.), or if standard syntax/Tree-sitter highlighting is not actively attached, your code will look flat, muted, or entirely uncolored.

Here is a ready-to-use prompt you can copy and paste to have the AI inspect and fix the issue while keeping your `ravenswing` theme:

***

```text
My code files (Python, C, Bash, Lua, etc.) lack syntax and keyword coloring in Neovim. I want rich syntax highlighting, but I do NOT want to change my current theme ("ravenswing")—I want to keep ravenswing intact.

Please analyze and fix the highlighting:
1. Check `~/.config/nvim/init.lua` and verify whether Tree-sitter highlighting is actually attaching to buffers and whether `syntax on` or `termguicolors` are configured properly.
2. Inspect the `ravenswing` colorscheme (check `~/.config/nvim/colors/ravenswing.*`). Determine if it is missing modern Tree-sitter capture groups (`@function`, `@keyword`, `@string`, `@type`, `@variable`, `@constant`, `@comment`, etc.) or if it lacks fallbacks to standard highlight groups (`Function`, `Keyword`, `String`, etc.).
3. Update or patch the configuration / colorscheme so that Tree-sitter captures are properly colored with distinct, complementary tones that fit the `ravenswing` palette (or linked to standard syntax highlights), ensuring Python, C, Bash, and Lua all have clear, distinct syntax coloring without breaking or replacing the theme.
4. Verify the fix in headless Neovim to confirm that highlight groups are active.
```
